issues: tests/helpers.py Book.fail overrides unittest.TestCase.fail, and assertIn, assertIsNone and assertEqual on lists or dicts all report through self.fail, so a failing assertion runs the CLI with the failure message as its arguments, gets argparse's exit code 2, and passes silently; test_api.test_bad_json_and_paths also calls self.fail('bad JSON was accepted') expecting the unittest version.

The schema is spread across modules: core.SCHEMA, banking.TABLES, invoicing.TABLES and reports.CLEARED are created lazily through tables(ctx) calls at the start of each handler, so read-only commands run DDL and it is easy to forget a call in a new handler.

banking.check_template repeats the validation in core.post_txn (posting count, blank amount, per-currency balance), even though core.py's header says not to duplicate its helpers, so the two rule sets can drift apart.

cli.main only catches UserError and sqlite3.Error, so a decimal InvalidOperation from q2 on a huge amount (for example '1e999999') or a ValueError from add_months past year 9999 ends in a traceback rather than exit 2; cli.run_args also contains dead code ('conn.executescript if False else None', 'if ... : pass').

banking.import_ and recurring_run write an audit entry only when they created something, while reconcile always writes one, so the 'one audit entry per successful data-changing command' rule is applied inconsistently.

api.serve commits and restarts the CLI's open transaction by hand (ctx.conn.execute('COMMIT'/'BEGIN')), the API rebuilds argv strings and the whole argparse parser for every request, and api.text accepts JSON floats for amounts, so the HTTP layer is tightly coupled to CLI internals.
strengths: Every command runs inside one explicit BEGIN/COMMIT with ROLLBACK on any exception, so failed commands (including whole imports or recurring runs that hit a closed period) leave nothing half-written.
Money handling is careful: Decimal stored as TEXT, a single q2/fmt pair for half-up rounding and the -0.00 fix, and every SQL query uses parameters.
The command registry (Registry.add with a read/write/admin permission tag) keeps permission checks in one place, and the CLI and HTTP API share the same handlers and documents.
